key_insight: Embedding trained neural networks into optimization models enables data-driven constraints and objective approximations, but smaller, sparser networks can make these models more practical to solve.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can incorporate empirically learned relationships into optimization while managing the computational cost of neural-network representations.
method: Train neural networks to represent constraints or approximate nonlinear objectives.
Embed the trained networks into optimization models.
Consider network size and sparsity to improve computational tractability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks, without specifying datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: Embedded neural networks may make optimization models too large or slow to solve, so predictive fit must be weighed against computational tractability.
paper_title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
